claims.statement: The only @SpringBootTest in the entire repository is EcshopxApplicationTests.contextLoads in ecshopx-bootstrap; every other test is a plain JUnit 5 unit/slice test that constructs classes directly with Mockito mocks and never boots a Spring context.

*DispatchFlowTest classes (200+ under ecshopx-bootstrap/src/test/java/cn/shopex/ecshopx/dispatch/) pin one message end to end: a real InMemoryDispatchRegistry holds the real handler/listener, a real DispatchFacade + DispatchFanOutPlanner + DispatchCore is built with the REDIS driver replaced by a message-capturing list (DispatchCore.asyncReady(registry, new SyncDispatchDriver(registry), Map.of(DispatchDriverType.REDIS, captured::add))), the captured DispatchMessage's queue/delay/listenerName/payload is asserted, and a real DispatchConsumerRuntime then consumes the message into the handler body.

Publish probes pin AFTER_COMMIT timing with a hand-rolled fake PlatformTransactionManager: getTransaction calls TransactionSynchronizationManager.initSynchronization(), commit iterates the registered synchronizations and invokes each afterCommit() before clearing; the service is driven through a TransactionTemplate over that manager, and the test asserts the dispatch publish fires only after commit (zero facade interactions inside the transaction), with an @AfterEach clearing TransactionSynchronizationManager between tests.

Consume-side envelopes are pinned by *EventAsyncConsumeTest (ecshopx-orders, ~50 classes) and *DispatchConsumerRuntimeTest (youshu/hfpay/reservation): the test hand-builds a DispatchMessage carrying the real listener name and queue, registers the real listener on an InMemoryDispatchRegistry with its production ListenerDispatchOptions, and drives DispatchConsumerRuntime.consume(msg, 1) to verify the listener's downstream service runs exactly once with the payload.

Controller tests (*WebSliceTest in bootstrap, *DelegationTest / *EndpointMappingTest / *WebMvcTest in bundles) use MockMvcBuilders.standaloneSetup(controller).setCustomArgumentResolvers(new FlexibleBodyMethodArgumentResolver(objectMapper, null)).build() — the production resolver must be registered manually because standalone setup has no Spring MVC infrastructure; operator identity is injected via .requestAttr(...) on the OperatorJwtRequestAttributes.OPERATOR_JWT_USER_DATA attribute, and DelegationTests additionally verifyNoMoreInteractions over all injected services to guard that controllers carry no dispatch-publisher path.

Unit tests that exercise services building MyBatis-Plus lambda wrappers register entity metadata manually in @BeforeAll via TableInfoHelper.initTableInfo(new MapperBuilderAssistant(new MybatisConfiguration(), ""), Entity.class) for each entity the mocked mapper will be called with — there is no live SqlSessionFactory in tests, so without this the wrapper construction throws.

Where a service genuinely needs Spring transaction proxies, tests use @SpringJUnitConfig with a hand-written @Configuration that @Imports the real service, declares every mapper/publisher/port as a Mockito mock() bean, and backs @EnableTransactionManagement with an H2 EmbeddedDatabaseBuilder DataSource plus DataSourceTransactionManager — H2 is a test-scoped dependency only in ecshopx-members, ecshopx-goods, and ecshopx-third-party, and the in-memory DB holds no tables (it exists solely so the transaction manager is real).

The repo's canonical verification commands are ./mvnw -pl <module> test (one Bundle), ./mvnw -pl <module> test -Dtest=ClassName (one class), and the pre-PR gate ./mvnw -pl <module> -am verify required by readme.md's contributing checklist; CONTRIBUTING.md additionally requires all tests to pass and new features to add test cases.

Production controllers document their own re-verification commands in Javadoc: WxappOrderController embeds exact mvn -pl ecshopx-orders -Dtest=...PublishProbeTest,...EventAsyncConsumeTest test invocations for the dispatch contracts each endpoint relies on.

No POM in the repository configures Surefire/Failsafe/JaCoCo or Testcontainers; the parent POM's build section only configures spring-boot-maven-plugin (skipped except in bootstrap) and flatten-maven-plugin, and test deps come solely from spring-boot-starter-test (plus H2 in three modules) — so ./mvnw test runs default Surefire behavior over *Test classes.

Bundle-local *PublishProbeTest / *BusProbeTest classes assert the publish side without HTTP or bus infrastructure: the real service runs with a mocked DispatchFacade (often through the real OrderProcessLogPublishPortImpl, whose publish defers to afterCommit via DispatchOptions.oplQueuedAfterCommit when a synchronization is active), and ArgumentCaptor + verify pin the message name, payload fields, and exact options tuple; some Spring-context variants set @TestPropertySource(properties = "ecshopx.h5.encrypt-sensitive-data=false") so captured payloads carry plain fixtures.

Inline in-memory dispatch stacks let @SpringJUnitConfig service tests assert real captured envelopes: a @TestConfiguration assembles InMemoryDispatchRegistry with the real listener registered, DispatchCore.asyncReady whose REDIS driver appends to a shared List<DispatchMessage>, a DispatchFanOutPlanner, a DispatchFacade, and a @Primary publisher bean — avoiding bootstrap's ~200 registration configs and duplicate-listener registration.

Dispatch bus internals are tested against mocked Redis/Rabbit templates: DispatchBusIntegrationTest proves the sync driver executes inline, RedisDispatchListener.poll() decodes a dispatch:default payload into runtime.consume, and the Rabbit listener does the same for AMQP bytes — queue draining, the delayed-ZSET mover, and poller loops are never run against real infrastructure.

Pure business rules get plain unit tests with mocked read ports and AssertJ: the AftersalesApplyCheckApplyService family pins PHP-aligned apply-check rules (freight validation against freight_fee, top-level refund fee/point ignored at check time) with error messages resolved through a StaticMessageSource test double (AftersalesTestMessageSource.FALLBACK, or a per-test source plus LocaleContextHolder), and @ConfigurationProperties validation is tested with Spring's ApplicationContextRunner (LanguePropertiesTest) — the one place the context runner appears.

Dispatch-flow tests are homed in ecshopx-bootstrap's test tree because bootstrap depends on every Bundle: the test can see both the bootstrap publisher implementation (config/ package) and the handler in any Bundle, and registry-level tests (DispatchBusConfigTest) boot only DispatchBusConfig with a mocked dispatchBusStringRedisTemplate to assert the core beans exist.

A negative variant of the *PublishProbeTest family pins publish absence for the deferred shopadmin create: ShopadminNormalOrderCreateOrchestratorNormalOrderAddDispatchPublishProbeTest and NormalOrderAdminCreateUserOrderServiceNormalOrderAddDispatchPublishProbeTest construct the real orchestrator (and the real NormalOrderAdminCreateUserOrderService over it) with all collaborators mocked and verify only preparePricingSnapshot plus ShopadminDeferredOrderCache.saveWaitPay(state, orderId, companyId, payType, totalFee, ttl) are invoked, returning order_id with order_status=NOTPAY — neither class holds a dispatch publisher, and the EVENT_NORMAL_ORDER_ADD publish moves to materialization (ShopadminDeferredOrderService.splitAndPublishOnce calls NormalOrderAddDispatchPublisher.publish only after payment persists the snapshot), so the probe pins absence plus the saveWaitPay call instead of a message name.

PHP-parity alignment tests (*AlignPhpTest, two classes) pin that Java order-create mirrors the legacy PHP OrderService::_formatOrderData behavior, citing it in their Javadoc: OrderCreatePersistencePortImplShopIdAlignPhpTest captures the NormalOrders, NormalOrdersItems and OrderAssociations inserts via ArgumentCaptor and asserts shop_id comes from orderData (0 when the shop check is off for normal/shopadmin) rather than being rewritten to distributor_id (which stays 104L), plus preassigned order-id reuse and default-currency fee fields; its goods-bundle twin OrderCreateFormatDataPortImplShopIdAlignPhpTest pins the same shop_id=0 rule on the format side, matching OrderCreatePersistencePortImpl's production comment 'PHP: shop_id from orderData (shopInfo; 0 when isCheckShopValid=false) — not distributor_id'.

Guard-relaxation tests pin that a deliberately loosened business rule stays relaxed while the surviving guard stays wired: SeckillActivityCreateServiceLimitedTimeSaleShopOverlapTest runs the real SeckillActivityCreateService create/update with seckillActivityMapper.selectList returning an overlapping same-shop limited_time_sale activity, wraps the call in assertDoesNotThrow (the shop mutex must not reject), and then verify(guard).checkActivityValidBySecKill(anyMap()) — consistent with the production code, which always builds guardParams with use_bound=1 so checkSecKill's use_bound=0 whole-store rejection branch is never entered on the seckill write path, while per-item overlap guarding remains active; the test also clears TransactionSynchronizationManager in @AfterEach because the @Transactional service registers after-commit synchronizations (salespersonItemsShelvesJobDispatchPublisher.publish).

*ScopeTest classes pin tenant scoping with plain Mockito: write-side probes (ItemsProfitSaveServiceScopeTest) prove a foreign item_id aborts the entire save with never() verifications on every repository write path, and read-side probes (OrderExportFilterAssemblerDistributorScopeTest) prove a distributor account's export filter is forced to the activated/JWT distributor_id (request parameters cannot override) while admin accounts get no forced scope.

*TableContractTest classes reflect over entity metadata instead of mocking behavior: PosStoreAccountTableContractTest asserts the @MpTable annotation on PosStoreAccount names table pos_store_account and declares exactly one unique index uk_employee_no(employee_no), and — only when local Flyway pos_store_account scripts exist (they are not committed by default) — that the incremental SQL keeps the same index, because @MpTable/@MpIndex are the schema contract MyBatis-Plus sees via MpMetadataAnnotationHandler.

The deferred shopadmin create path is pinned by a negative publish probe: ShopadminNormalOrderCreateOrchestratorNormalOrderAddDispatchPublishProbeTest drives the real orchestrator with mocked ports and verifies only preparePricingSnapshot plus saveWaitPay (order id, company, pay type, total fee, TTL), returning order_id and order_status NOTPAY with no normal_order_add dispatch publish at create time.

The security-hardening window added a family of plain-Mockito tests that pin tenant-scoping (company/distributor) guards across nearly every bundle (adapay, aftersales, ali, bspay, comments, companys, data-cube, distribution, employee-purchase, espier, form, goods, kujiale, members, orders, promotions, salesperson, selfservice, work-wechat, wsugc), reusing the standard harness (real service constructed with new, mocked mappers/Redis/ports, @BeforeAll TableInfoHelper.initTableInfo) but asserting an authorization guard rather than a dispatch tuple; class Javadoc cites the ECX-108xx/109xx ticket.

Distributor-list scope tests pin JWT/activated-shop clamping: AftersalesRefundListDistributorScopeTest builds a JWT with distributor_ids [10,20], feeds an unauthorized distributorIdRaw (or an empty activated-shop intersection), and captures the selectCount LambdaQueryWrapper to assert its params bind the JWT shops (10L, 20L) rather than the requested shop; the authorized-id case pins that exactly that one shop is bound, and AftersalesRefundLogExportDistributorScopeTest pins the same clamp on the export-filter map.

Company-scope tests pin cross-tenant write rejection with two assertion shapes: SQL-segment scoping (EmployeePurchaseActivityItemWriteServiceCompanyScopeTest captures the selectOne wrapper and asserts its SQL segment contains company_id, then uses a thenAnswer that returns a foreign-company row only when the wrapper lacks the company_id clause, proving a correctly-scoped query never sees it, with never() on every write path), and name-collision rejection (WorkWechatVerifyDomainFileServiceCompanyScopeTest proves a same-name row owned by another company makes the write throw with never() on updateById/insert, and the own-company update keeps the original company_id in the captured entity).

*OwnershipTest classes pin front-endpoint self-service ownership with no side effects on rejection: RightsFrontWxappGetRightsCodeOwnershipTest proves a foreign-user/foreign-company/missing rights row throws ResourceException(无权访问该权益) with never() on both downstream effectors (wechatStringRedisTemplate.opsForValue and the barcode-generate service), WxappOfflinePaymentGetVoucherOwnerScopeTest proves another user's order returns an empty list and never touches the voucher mapper, and MembersControllerAddressBuyUserScopeTest pins that a foreign buy_user_id is rejected while a self/missing one resolves to the auth user.

AdapayDepositTradeRechargeCallbackServiceIdempotencyTest pins the deposit-recharge callback's atomic takeover: the update wrapper's SQL segment carries a trade_status guard (so the transition is guarded by trade_status), a lost race (update returns 0) throws ResourceException(更新已处理，不需要更新) with zero side effects (never() on the balance mutation, verifyNoInteractions on Redis and the SMS publisher), and the first-callback success path applies the deposit balance mutation exactly once with the right amounts.

Two *ReplayGuardTest classes pin Redis SET NX replay guards with an identical shape (mocked StringRedisTemplate whose setIfAbsent result decides admission): OpenapiSignedRequestReplayGuardTest proves first-acquire accepts with an openapi:auth:replay:-prefixed key while already-seen, missing app_key/sign/timestamp, and a Redis exception all reject (fail-closed); InboundSignedCallbackReplayGuardTest adds a freshness window via an injectable nowMsSupplier clock (a timestamp older than the skew is rejected) and a shuyun:cb:replay:-prefixed key.

AdapayDepositTradeRechargeCallbackServiceSmsDispatchTest pins a dispatch publish after commit using the fake-transaction idiom: the service is driven through a TransactionTemplate over a Mockito-stubbed PlatformTransactionManager (getTransaction calls initSynchronization, commit fires each afterCommit then clears), asserts verifyNoInteractions(publisher) inside the transaction body and exactly one publishRechargeSendSmsNotice(10L, 20L, mobile, money) after commit, and proves a non-SUCCESS status never touches the publisher.
